clue.text: Begin with a pre-eminent sales promoter

parts.note: someone pre-eminent is a star, the leading performer
a tout drums up custom, selling tickets or touting for business

explanation.surface: Advice to launch a career alongside a top-flight salesman.
explanation.definitionFit: To set off on a journey or venture is to commence it.

clue.text: Heavy type put on by one who wishes to hide his fear

definitions.text: put on by one who wishes to hide his fear

explanation.surface: A heavy printing face, or the brave look a frightened person assumes.
explanation.definitionFit: Printers call thick dark lettering by this name, and a brave front is the expression a coward wears to conceal terror.

clue.text: Darkly pigmented skin blemish to be embarrassed about

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shy word goes round the blemish

parts.note: embarrassed people are shy, bashful
a wart is a small growth or blemish on the skin

explanation.surface: Someone is self-conscious about a dark mark on their skin.
explanation.definitionFit: A swarthy complexion is dusky, with dark skin tone.

clue.text: One who declares old currency

explanation.surface: A person who makes declarations, and a coin of antiquity.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who states things is literally a stater; the stater was also an ancient Greek gold or silver coin.

clue.text: Aero-engine manufacturer invested in coal as a stockholder

indicators.note: invested in means placed inside, so the maker's letters are put within the fuel word

parts.note: taken as written
RR stands for Rolls-Royce, maker of aircraft engines

explanation.surface: A jet-engine firm puts money into the coal industry as an investor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stockholder' reads as a shareholder, but here it is a pen holding livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: A corral is an enclosure that holds cattle or horses, so it literally holds stock.

clue.text: Tea-time question applying equally to the haves and have nots

definitions.text: Tea-time question applying equally to the haves and have nots

parts.words: Tea-time question applying equally to the haves and have nots
parts.note: a host pouring tea asks whether you want milk added or not, and the phrase covers both those who have it and those who do not

explanation.surface: A question at tea that sounds like a remark on rich and poor.
explanation.definitionFit: Hosts ask guests whether they take milk in tea, a question covering both choices.

clue.text: Well could it be called a seaside resort

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a spring might be called a coastal holiday town.
explanation.definitionFit: A well is a spot where animals or people drink; a spa or coastal town visited for its waters also bears this name.

clue.text: WWI conflict in which soldiers had the ground cut from under their feet?

definitions.text: WWI conflict in which soldiers had the ground cut from under their feet?

parts.words: WWI conflict in which soldiers had the ground cut from under their feet?
parts.note: the idiom of losing one's footing is taken literally: soldiers fought from ditches dug into the earth beneath them

explanation.surface: First World War fighting where troops were undermined.
explanation.definitionFit: The Western Front was fought from dug-out lines in the earth, the defining style of that war.

clue.text: Looked hard for a leftish newspaper chief

parts.note: the Morning Star is a British left-wing daily paper
ED is short for editor, the chief of a newspaper

explanation.surface: Searching intently for the boss of a left-leaning paper.
explanation.definitionFit: To gaze fixedly at something is to look intently.

clue.text: Honoured by the electorate but dishonoured by the bank

explanation.surface: Voters honour someone whom the bank refuses.
explanation.definitionFit: An MP elected to Parliament is said to be sent back by voters; a cheque the bank refuses to pay is sent back unpaid.

clue.text: Well could it be called seizure

explanation.surface: Wondering whether good health might be called an attack.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone healthy is in good shape; an epileptic attack or convulsion is also called this.

clue.text: Dark circle has unusual role in motoring club

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters within the motoring club's letters

parts.note: AA is the Automobile Association, a British motoring organisation

indicators.note: unusual signals the letters of role are put into an unusual order

explanation.surface: A sinister ring takes on a strange part in a motoring organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dark circle' suggests shadows under the eyes, but this is the anatomical ring around a nipple.
explanation.definitionFit: The ring of darker skin around a nipple is called this in anatomy.

clue.text: No easy fortune comes the way of those who suffer it

definitions.text: No easy fortune comes the way of those who suffer it

parts.words: No easy fortune comes the way of those who suffer it
parts.note: difficult fate, the opposite of an easy ride, is what unlucky people endure

explanation.surface: Unlucky people never get a comfortable windfall.
explanation.definitionFit: Misfortune is a tough break, a fate that is not easy.

clue.text: Returnable cheque

parts.note: a bad cheque gets returned by the bank, and the word also reads the same in either direction

explanation.surface: A cheque that can be sent back.
explanation.definitionFit: A worthless cheque that bounces is described by slang meaning useless.

clue.text: Patience-tiring pests should be told to get it all tied up

definitions.text: Patience-tiring pests should be told to get it

explanation.surface: Annoying people should be told to wrap themselves up.
explanation.walkthrough: "Get knotted!" is a British put-down meaning go away.
explanation.definitionFit: "Get knotted" is a rude British brush-off for a nuisance; tangled string is likewise tied in loops.

clue.text: Draw a game that is not played

definitions.text: Draw a game that is not played

parts.words: Draw a game that is not played
parts.note: the equal result is a draw, yet the word also names a cup fixture drawn out of a hat before anyone plays it

explanation.surface: Picking out a match yet to be contested.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawn match ends level, and a cup fixture is also named this when the draw is made.

clue.text: Airline has to wend back South-and it is said to travel fast

definitions.text: it is said to travel fast

parts.note: BA is British Airways

indicators.note: back means the word wend is read in reverse order

parts.note: S is the compass abbreviation for South

explanation.surface: An airline must fly back south, and word of it spreads quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns WEND into DNEW. The definition plays on the proverb that ill tidings travel fast.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says unwelcome tidings spread quickly.

clue.text: Made over in the form of a duly executed document

definitions.text: in the form of a duly executed document

explanation.surface: Property transferred by means of a properly signed deed.
explanation.definitionFit: Property transferred to someone is legally made over; split in two the word reads as signed, the state of an executed deed.

clue.text: No arctic change has a soporific effect

definitions.note: the definition describes the adjective's sense, inducing sleep or stupor

indicators.note: change tells the solver the letters of no arctic must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Polar weather that stays the same makes everyone drowsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Opiates and similar drugs dull the senses and induce sleep.

clue.text: Sell pet remedy against slugs

indicators.note: remedy means put right, so the letters of sell pet are rearranged into a correct order

explanation.surface: Offering a pet cure for garden molluscs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slugs' looks like the garden pests, but means small shot, as fired from an airgun.
explanation.definitionFit: Slugs are small bullets or shot, and so are these small balls of lead.

clue.text: The order in which one likes everything to be-except a bed

definitions.text: The order in which one likes everything to be-except a bed

parts.words: The order in which one likes everything to be-except a bed
parts.note: the phrase for perfect neatness also names a prank bed with the sheets folded so one cannot get in

explanation.surface: Everything should be neat and tidy, but not the bed.
explanation.walkthrough: An apple-pie bed is a schoolboy prank: the sheet is folded so the sleeper's legs cannot stretch out.
explanation.definitionFit: Perfect tidiness is described as apple-pie order, while a prank bed shares the name.

clue.text: Fellow abandons Londoners who keep to themselves

indicators.note: abandons means the fellow leaves, so his letters are taken out of the city dwellers

parts.note: a don is a university fellow

explanation.surface: A man walks out on the people of the capital, who are unsociable.
explanation.definitionFit: Solitary people who avoid company are those who keep to themselves.

clue.text: Changing shapes of the moon

indicators.note: changing signals that the letters of shapes are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: The moon's waxing and waning forms.
explanation.definitionFit: The moon's monthly stages, from new to full, are its varying appearances.

clue.text: Avant-garde playwright mentioned in Paris art review

indicators.note: mentioned in says the name sits inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A radical dramatist gets a mention in a Parisian art critique.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Paul Sartre was a French existentialist dramatist, author of Huis Clos.

clue.text: Leisurely start to an Hawaiian welcome

indicators.note: start to points to the opening letters of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A relaxed beginning to a reception in Hawaii.
explanation.definitionFit: Visitors to Hawaii are traditionally greeted with a garland of flowers placed round the neck.

clue.text: Artist in autumn shower

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
taken as written
fall is the American word for autumn

explanation.surface: A painter caught in an autumn downpour.
explanation.definitionFit: A shower is a brief spell of precipitation.

clue.text: For all the world like an American lass swallowing a highball

indicators.note: swallowing means taking in, so the girl goes round the high shot

parts.note: gal is American slang for a girl
a lob is a ball hit high in the air, as in tennis

explanation.surface: Resembling a US girl gulping a whisky cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'highball' looks like the drink, but is a lofted shot.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worldwide applies everywhere on earth.

clue.text: Sincere wish and pledge of French father

parts.note: an earnest is a token payment or pledge of good faith
de is French for of
sire means father, especially of an animal

explanation.surface: A heartfelt hope backed by a Frenchman's father's promise.
explanation.definitionFit: A heartfelt longing is a sincere wish.
